rubric.why: Identifies that the error is in the program's logic and causes an incorrect result.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the program's reasoning or logic is faulty.

rubric.why: Distinguishes a logical error from a syntax error.
rubric.description: Program runs without a syntax error but gives an incorrect result
rubric.how: Award for explaining that the program may run but does not produce the intended result.

modelAnswer: A logical error is a mistake in the logic of a program.
The program may run, but it produces an incorrect result.

rubric.why: Names the table and its relation to program variables.
rubric.description: A table used to record variable values
rubric.how: Award for identifying that values of variables are written in a table.

rubric.why: Explains that the values are followed as the program executes.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the table follows variable changes step by step.

modelAnswer: A trace table is a table used to record the values of variables as a program executes.
It helps follow the program step by step and find errors.

items.followUp: What does the “Draw a diagram” strategy help us do when defining a problem?

rubric.why: States that the strategy involves making a guess or estimate about a solution.
rubric.description: Make a sensible guess or estimate
rubric.how: Award for describing the use of a reasonable guess about the answer or solution.

rubric.why: Shows that the guess is checked against the problem's information or requirements.
rubric.description: Check the guess against the problem
rubric.how: Award for stating that the guess should be tested or verified using the given information.

modelAnswer: The “Use Guess” strategy means making a sensible guess or estimate about the solution.
The guess is then checked against the given information and requirements of the problem.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of drawing a flowchart while planning a solution?

rubric.why: Identifies drawing as a way to create a preliminary representation of the solution.
rubric.description: Draw a rough prototype or sketch
rubric.how: Award for stating that a preliminary drawing or sketch is made.

rubric.why: Explains that the drawing helps visualize the proposed solution.
rubric.description: Visualize or understand the proposed solution
rubric.how: Award for stating that the drawing helps plan or view how the solution will look.

modelAnswer: The Prototype (Draw) technique involves making a rough drawing or sketch of the proposed solution.
The drawing helps visualize and plan the solution before it is developed.

items.followUp: Give one example of an empty HTML tag.

rubric.why: Names the type of tag that has an opening and a closing tag.
Names the type of tag that does not require a closing tag.

modelAnswer: The two types of HTML tags are paired (container) tags and unpaired (empty) tags.

items.followUp: What information is placed in the body section of an HTML document?

rubric.why: Identifies the head section and its HTML boundaries.
rubric.description: The section between the head tags
rubric.how: Award for identifying the section enclosed by <head> and </head>.

rubric.why: Describes the kind of information contained in the head section.
rubric.description: Contains the document title and other page information
rubric.how: Award for mentioning the title or other information about the document, generally not displayed as page content.

modelAnswer: The head section is the part of an HTML document enclosed by <head> and </head>.
It contains information about the document, such as its title, rather than the main page content.

rubric.why: Correctly converts the hexadecimal digit A to its four-bit binary equivalent.
Correctly converts the remaining digits and gives the combined binary number.
rubric.description: Convert and combine the remaining digits
rubric.how: Award for the correct four-bit conversions and final binary answer.

items.followUp: Write the names of the arithmetic operators used in programming.

rubric.why: Includes the other two standard logical operators.
rubric.how: Award for naming both OR and NOT.

modelAnswer: The logical operators are AND, OR, and NOT.
